Stationarity differentiates chords before applying the caustic constraint. The common eccentric-angle shift holds half-width fixed, giving a term proportional to S_i C_i, while total perimeter gives the C_i² mean. The reflection-law calculation works even for star polygons.

Direct Cramer systems about the focus and opposite-edge pair yield the printed coefficient; U²−c²C²/a²=(b²−λ)D²>0. Averaging over all edges counts pair members twice. Opposite terms cancel exactly for the center.

A repeated odd triangle explicitly keeps its original nonzero centroid. Near-degenerate caustics, hyperbolic caustics, area centroids, different polygons, and nonprimitive even labels are outside the claim.
